identity.title: Studio Settings module tab, feature subtabs and Engine Profiles binding inside Handshake Settings

context_capsule.authored_by: Studio lead (KERNEL_BUILDER) on Operator instruction 2026-10-30 (plan PW-10)

closure_unit.outcome: Give Studio one Settings tab inside Handshake Settings with one subtab per module that owns a user-facing setting (brush, fill, selection, render preference, export stage, audio device, import profiles), every entry registered through the host preference schema with a stable id that AccessKit, the UserManual, the structured model tools and diagnostics share; Engine Profiles (render CPU/GPU provider, budgets) is selected and dispatched inside Settings with immutable revision identity and current authorization; search over settings uses canonical Handpick. No parallel settings store, no per-tool structs reachable only from CLI flags.

materialized_acceptance.text: Every Studio module with a user-facing setting has a reachable subtab under the Studio tab; a test walks the tree and finds every registered entry by keyboard and by stable id (GUI-DESKTOP-014/015/018).

Settings entries are registered through the host preference schema (PreferenceSchemaEntry-compatible) and nowhere else; the CLI flags that set them today map onto the same entries (GUI-DESKTOP-016/017).

Engine Profiles for Studio render providers lives inside Settings: complete-profile selection, dispatch, immutable revision identity and current authorization are proved; the host adoption of Engine Profiles (WP-KERNEL-012 MT-196) is consumed, not re-implemented (GUI-DESKTOP-019).
Handpick is the settings search: native mount, keyboard, focus and dismissal proved (GUI-DESKTOP-013).
Loading, empty, denied and error states of the Settings tab are truthful and usable; the model view does not steal operator focus (GUI-DESKTOP-012/045).
